newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to investigate Megawati's lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to investigate Megawati's lawyer.

text.p: Indonesia is investigating whether ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri's chief lawyer has overstepped his legal role, the Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.

"We are researching whether the statements R.O. Tambunan has made are connected with his profession or cases which are before the courts or outside this and for his own personal interests," Justice Minister Utoyo Usman was quoted as telling reporters in Denpasar, Bali, on Monday.

It it were proved that the sometimes flamboyant and outspoken Tambunan was helping conduct political manoeuvres he could be brought before a lawyers' council or face unspecified sanctions outside his profession.

Tambunan, the head of a group of lawyers known as the Team for the Defence of Democracy, has led a number of high-profile lawsuits linked to Megawati, who was ousted as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party in June by a government-backed congress.
His comments on the cases have received widespread media coverage both in Indonesia and overseas.
Tambunan has been the lead lawyer in Megawati's lawsuit against the armed forces chief, the interior minister and the national police chief for backing the rebel congress.
A Jakarta sessions court dismissed the case last week saying it was not in its jurisdiction. Megawati has appealed to the high court.

Tambunan has also led cases against the General Election Institute (LPU) for not accepting a list of Megawati's candidates for next year's parliamentary elections and the East Jakarta mayor for sealing a temporary office set up by Megawati supporters.
He has also appeared in two of the 10 separate trials of Megawati supporters who have been accused of assault and disobeying police orders during a police raid on the PDI headquarters on July 27.
The raid triggered riots in Jakarta in which at least five people died and scores of buildings and vehicles were set ablaze. It was the worst violence in the city for more than two decades.
